title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy value without cross-origin isolation
description: The response declares a Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy value that does not isolate the browsing context from its opener: `unsafe-none` (the default) or `same-origin-allow-popups` both keep opener access for some navigation, so a cross-origin page can retain a reference to this window.
remediation: Immediate: send `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` on application documents so a cross-origin opener cannot retain a handle to the window. Durable: set the header once for the whole application and review OAuth and payment popups, which need `same-origin-allow-popups` instead. Trade-off: `same-origin` severs the `window.opener` relationship some sign-in and checkout flows rely on, so choose the stricter value per route rather than globally.
limitation: Value check on the COOP token. `same-origin` and `noopener-allow-popups` are isolation modes and are not reported; an empty value is not reported here because a missing or empty header is DPK-DAST-012. The explicit `unsafe-none` token is also reported by DPK-DAST-076, which asks the narrower question "is the default opt-out spelled out?"; both fire on that value by design, so read them together. The rule reads one response and cannot confirm that an opener relationship exists.
